The '''2022—23 Ligue 1''' was a season of top-flight football in [[Ivory Coast]].

The league expanded from 14 to 16 teams, and the federation also announced a four-team playoff to end the regular season. However, the federation ended up cancelling the play-off after the season, giving ASEC Mimosas their 29th overall title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ami-sportif.com/2023/06/21/football-lasec-mimosas-sacree-championne-de-cote-divoire-pour-la-29e-fois/|title=Football : L’Asec Mimosas sacrée championne de Côte d’Ivoire pour la 29e fois !|date=21 June 2023|language=fr|publisher=Ami-sportif}}</ref> Since teams would have taken half of their points into the six-game rectangular play-off, Mimosas would have started with around a four-point lead.<ref name="mondial">{{cite web|url=https://mondialsport.ci/ligue-1-lonaci-l-asec-termine-la-saison-reguliere-en-tete-l-usc-bassam-et-l-es-bafing-relegues-22550.sport|title=Ligue 1 LONACI : L’ASEC termine la saison régulière en tête, l’USC Bassam et l’ES Bafing relégués|language=fr|date=11 June 2023|publisher=Mondial Sport}}</ref>

ES Bafing were relegated on the final day of the season despite starting the round outside the relegation zone and drawing AFAD 0–0, who also needed a win to guarantee their spot in the cancelled play-off, but were leaped by ASI d'Abengourou who won their final match of the season.<ref name="mondial"/>

AFAD Djékanou qualified for the Confederation Cup as the cup runners-up.
